Name: Hugh Latimer
Summary: English bishop and preacher (c. 1487-1555) whose plain, searching sermons made him one of the most loved voices of the English Reformation.
Contribution: As bishop of Worcester and court preacher under Edward VI, he preached against corruption and for reform in language ordinary people understood, and his sermons remain models of English preaching.
Testimony: Under Mary I he was condemned and burned at the stake in Oxford alongside Nicholas Ridley, urging his fellow sufferer to be of good comfort.
